mechanism_narrative: The recent sustained decline in RETAIL_REC mobility, observed over the last two weeks, indicates a persistent negative trend in consumer activity that will continue to depress retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility shows a significant recovery, rising above -20% from baseline, it will signal increased office presence and associated lunchtime or after-work retail activity, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -20% but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than over the last 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM activity suggests a continued preference for local, essential outings and staying home, which will suppress non-essential RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL and GROCERY_PHARM remain stable but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases.

mechanism_narrative: As spring progresses, increasing PARKS mobility, especially if it recovers from recent dips, will divert recreational activity away from indoor retail, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, assuming no new restrictions.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility rises above 0% from baseline
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above 0% but RETAIL_REC also increases over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent stagnation in TRANSIT stations mobility, hovering around -28% for the past three weeks, indicates a lack of return to public transport use, which will continue to limit access to and thus depress RETAIL_REC in urban centers over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility remains stagnant but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases significantly.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, falling below 9% from baseline, would indicate people spending less time at home and more time out, which is likely to translate into increased RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 9% but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days decreases or remains flat.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, indicating a broader return to office work and associated commuting, will drive a positive rebound in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as more people frequent commercial areas.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increase by more than 2 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains stable or slightly declines while RETAIL_REC is also declining, it suggests a general cautious consumer sentiment where even essential outings are not increasing, reinforcing the negative trend for non-essential retail over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains stable or declines, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days shows a significant increase.
